brief: BofA and Morgan Stanley data show the cost of building a US AI data center has risen from about $30 billion per gigawatt in 2022/23 to $49 billion now, with MS projecting $50-60 billion by 2030. The author's own scenarios, run off BofA's $49 billion starting point, range from $60 billion (steady 8% a year inflation) to $76 billion (if MS's surveyed +15% a year holds for two years) by 2030. IT equipment is 78% of the build, and memory, which MS calls the newest driver of inflation, has risen more than six-fold in a year. Rising build costs are pushing AI debt issuance higher ($471 billion in 2026 versus $216 billion in 2025, per MS), and credit markets are becoming more selective, pushing lower-rated hyperscalers and neoclouds toward secured, asset-level financing. The author expects the bond market to force builders to either slow capacity or absorb the costs, and views MS's 240 GW bear-case 2030 capacity forecast as more likely than its 377 GW bull case. Separately, despite power being only about 5% of build cost, it remains the binding bottleneck, with a projected 70 GW US power shortfall by 2028 driving a shift toward on-site, behind-the-meter gas power.
